title: The stand that crossed the chalk line
public_context: Concert halls often keep incident forms alongside set lists and stage diagrams. The following fictional report comes from a small venue's winter series and concerns a touring instrumental group. Its setting includes familiar stage equipment, musicians, and a live concert.
source_title: Wren Hall performance incident card, winter series
source_text:
The incident card was completed after the Belltide Brass concert in Wren Hall's downstairs room. The group played two trumpets, horn, and trombone from a shallow riser. A weighted music stand held the trombone part just inside a chalk line marking the orchestra edge. Before doors opened, the stagehand checked the stand collar and left the floor cable loop behind the riser.

During the third piece, the stand moved toward the edge and the score pages slid over its shelf. The trombonist kept the final phrase from memory until the group reached the cadence. The conductor held the players there while a stagehand retrieved the pages and reset the stand behind the chalk line. The card gives no explanation for the stand's movement, and it does not blame the cable.

The crew paused the house lights for a short reset. The set list identifies the third piece as a slow fugue and has a penciled box around its later pickup. The horn player pointed to that mark while the trombonist checked the recovered pages, and the conductor waited until all four stands were ready. The players resumed at the next written pickup rather than repeating the third piece from its beginning. The trombonist checked the page order while the other musicians held their instruments at rest. The stagehand tightened the locking collar, then the conductor gave the downbeat. The remaining program continued in its printed order, including the planned final march. The report records no change to the remaining program order.

After the audience left, the stagehand found the collar screw partly backed out but not broken. The crew tightened it and attached a yellow service tag to the stand before returning it to the equipment cupboard. No instrument touched the riser rail, and nobody was injured. The hall report lists the interruption as less than two minutes, based on the stage clock; it does not give a precise restart time.

The card is clipped to the brass group's set list and a sketch of the riser. The sketch shows the chalk line, the stand, and the cable loop, but no measurement from the stand base to the edge. The trombonist signed the card after reading it. The service tag has no second inspection mark, and the next booking sheet names a different ensemble.
